context_notes: Managers approve up to 5 consecutive days. Anything over 10 consecutive days needs the CEO. She wants the tool to be Slack-first and simple. No more than 2 people out on the same team at once.

Policy: 20 PTO days and 5 sick days per year. PTO requests of 3 or more consecutive days need 2 weeks notice. Sick days need no notice. Max 5 unused PTO days carry over to the next year. Company holidays are tracked separately and don't count against PTO.

PTO accrues at about 1.67 days per month. Balances currently live in a Google Sheet called PTO Balances. Payroll runs on the 1st and 15th and needs a CSV export of approved days. Unused days above the carryover cap are forfeited on Dec 31.
Internal tools should be a single-page web app in TypeScript with Google Workspace login. No new paid vendors. Employee data must not be exposed publicly. Keep the codebase small and tested.

Suggested data model: requests(id, employee_email, start_date, end_date, type, status, approver_email, created_at). Status values: pending, approved, denied, cancelled. Prefers a small repo with unit tests for the day-counting and balance logic.
Wants a team calendar view showing who is out, with a mobile-friendly layout and keyboard accessibility. Counting days must skip weekends and company holidays.
Brand: teal accent (#0F766E), Inter font, lots of white space. Status colors: pending amber, approved green, denied red. One primary action per screen.
Sales cannot take PTO during the last two weeks of each quarter without his approval. He wants to see the sales team's requests before approving.
At least one Customer Success person must be working at all times. She needs to see overlaps on a team calendar before approving.
Can add a /timeoff Slack slash command and sync approved days to Google Calendar. Slack notifications should go to the approver and the requester.
